answer: Seeded Vertex Assignment. Each epoch, a public verifiable random function derives a secret permutation; agents are assigned a random vertex in an interaction graph only after committing a kernel of their action, so the seed is unknowable when identities are created. A walnut-sized proof-of-work must accompany each new identity, and the seed binds registrations to unpredictable slots, so precomputing placements fails. Attacker cost: one fresh proof-of-work plus registration per identity per epoch, scaling linearly and non-amortizable.
